title: Professional Communication
subtitle: Write plainly, communicate with stakeholders and share findings people act on.
outcomes: Write in plain language for any audience
Write effective emails, messages and letters
Give feedback and present findings clearly

pool.q: What is the first rule of plain language?
options: Use as few words as possible
Always write in the first person
pool.explain: Know who you are writing for and what they need to do.
pool.evidence: The first rule of plain language is: write for your audience

pool.q: What is one of the most common myths about plain language?
options: That you have to 'dumb down' your content so everyone can read it
That it only applies to legal documents
pool.explain: Plain language is clear, not simplistic — experts prefer it too.
pool.evidence: One of the most common plain language myths is that you have to “dumb down” your content so that everyone can read it.

pool.q: Why should you use the active voice?
options: It makes it clear who should do what
pool.explain: 'You must send the form' is clearer than 'The form must be sent'.
pool.evidence: Active voice makes it clear who should do what.

pool.q: When should you write for 8th graders?
options: Only if your audience actually is an 8th-grade class
pool.explain: Plain language means writing for your real audience, not dumbing everything down.
pool.evidence: Only write for 8th graders if your audience is, in fact, an 8th-grade class.

pool.q: Why should you limit the conditional and future tense?
options: They are banned in government writing
The more you use them, the harder readers must work to understand you
pool.explain: Present tense and active voice are easier to follow.
pool.evidence: The more you use conditional or future tense, the harder your audience has to work to understand your meaning.

pool.q: How can you help readers notice important information?
options: Add useful headings and lists, tables and visuals
Put key points at the very end
pool.explain: Design elements help people scan, read and understand.
pool.evidence: adding useful headings and lists, as well as tables and visuals, can help emphasize important information in your writing.

pool.q: Why does the guide advise against writing whole passages in capital letters?
options: It draws attention but makes text harder to read
pool.explain: Use bold or italics for important points instead.
pool.evidence: ALTHOUGH IT MAY DRAW THE USER’S ATTENTION TO THE SECTION, IT MAKES IT HARDER TO READ.

pool.q: What is 'iteration' when testing your content?
options: Writing a second draft without testing
pool.explain: Iteration is part of what makes usability testing effective.
pool.evidence: This process of testing, revising, and re-testing is called “iteration

pool.q: What should you always consider before sending someone a letter?
options: Whether to send it by recorded delivery
Whether a phone call would be cheaper
Whether you can send an email or text message instead
pool.explain: Digital messages are faster and cheaper when they meet the user's need.
pool.evidence: Always consider whether you can send an email or text message instead of a letter.

pool.q: Which two types of email or text message meet a user need?
pool.explain: Transactional messages confirm what the user did; subscriptions keep them updated.
pool.evidence: Two types of message that meet a user need are transactional messages and subscription messages.

pool.q: You send an email because the user completed an action. When should it arrive?
options: At the end of the week
Only if the user asks for it
pool.explain: An instant confirmation reassures users the action worked.
pool.evidence: automate the sending so that the user gets it straight away

pool.q: Where in a service should you look for moments to send reassuring messages?
options: The points where users are likely to get anxious
Wherever marketing wants to promote something
pool.explain: Look at the service end to end, from the user's point of view.
pool.evidence: Look at your service end to end and find the points where users are likely to get anxious.

pool.q: Why must letters from a service be especially clear?
options: They are often about something the user has never heard of or did not know they needed to do
pool.explain: Clarity matters most when the reader has to act or learn a new concept.
pool.evidence: A letter will often be about a thing the user’s never heard of or did not know they needed to do.

pool.q: How should a service decide how to contact its users?
options: Offer a choice, and stick to a stated preference where possible
pool.explain: A preferred format may be the one that is most accessible for that user.
pool.evidence: it’s good to offer your users a choice of how they’d like to be contacted

pool.q: Which service does the guidance suggest for sending letters to users?
pool.explain: Notify sends emails, text messages and letters for government services.
pool.evidence: you should consider using GOV.UK Notify to send letters to your users

pool.q: Who are a project's stakeholders?
options: Only the people who pay for it
People actively involved in the work or who have something to gain or lose from the project
pool.explain: Even if all deliverables are met, unhappy key stakeholders mean an unsuccessful project.
pool.evidence: They are the people who are actively involved with the work of the project or have something to either gain or lose as a result of the project.

pool.q: In a project to add lanes to a highway, how are motorists described?
options: As people who are not stakeholders
As members of the project team
As stakeholders who are positively affected
pool.explain: Stakeholders include anyone who gains or loses from the project.
pool.evidence: When you manage a project to add lanes to a highway, motorists are stakeholders who are positively affected.

pool.q: All deliverables are met, but key stakeholders are unhappy. How does the book judge this?
options: The project is a complete success
Stakeholders stop mattering once objectives are met
Nobody's happy — stakeholder satisfaction matters too
pool.explain: Meeting objectives is not enough if key stakeholders are dissatisfied.
pool.evidence: Even if all the deliverables are met and the objectives are satisfied, if your key stakeholders aren’t happy, nobody’s happy.

pool.q: Why can borrowed project team members be difficult to manage?
options: They don't report to you, so their priorities may be elsewhere
They cost more than permanent staff
pool.explain: Involving them in planning builds commitment.
pool.evidence: Because project team members are borrowed and they don’t report to you, their priorities may be elsewhere.

pool.q: What is a stakeholder analysis?
options: An assessment of a project's key participants and how it affects their problems and needs
A customer satisfaction survey after launch
A list of the team's skills
pool.explain: It also defines roles and reveals conflicts of interest between groups.
pool.evidence: Conduct a stakeholder analysis, or an assessment of a project’s key participants, and how the project will affect their problems and needs.

pool.q: When identifying stakeholders, whom should you include?
options: Those impacted by the project and groups able to impact it
pool.explain: Influence runs both ways.
pool.evidence: Include those who are impacted by the project, as well as groups with the ability to impact the project.

pool.q: How does a stakeholder's influence relate to the support a project manager needs from them?
options: The more influential they are, the more their support is needed
pool.explain: Lukewarm support from a powerful stakeholder can outweigh strong support from a weak one.
pool.evidence: The more influential a stakeholder is, the more a project manager will need their support.

pool.q: Why gather stakeholders' definitions of success at the start?
options: So they shape the objectives and stakeholders support the final outcome
So the team can decide alone
pool.explain: Discovering a mismatch at the end is a formula for failure.
pool.evidence: Gather definitions up front and include them in the objectives to help ensure that all stakeholders will be supportive of the final outcomes.

pool.q: What can regular communication do when you have bad news to share?
pool.explain: Stakeholders who are kept informed are less surprised by problems.
pool.evidence: may even soften the blow when you have bad news to share

pool.q: Roughly how much of a project manager's job is spent on communication?
pool.explain: That is why a communication plan is essential.
pool.evidence: 90% of a project manager’s job is spent on communication

pool.q: What is the first step in defining a communication plan?
options: Working out what communication stakeholders need from the project to make good decisions
pool.explain: Plan the content, format and timing around stakeholders' decisions.
pool.evidence: The first step in defining your communication plan is figuring out what kind of communication your stakeholders need from the project so they can make good decisions.

pool.q: What are teams that work together mainly through electronic communication called?
pool.explain: Virtual teams need especially clear communication plans.
pool.evidence: called virtual teams

pool.q: How much information should stakeholders receive?
options: Enough to stay informed and decide well, without being buried
Nothing until there is a problem
pool.explain: A communication plan matches information to each stakeholder's needs.
pool.evidence: The point is that you don’t want to bury stakeholders in too much information but you do want to give them enough so that they’re informed and can make appropriate decisions.

pool.q: What is Net Promoter Score (NPS)?
options: A measure of how customers talk about a company and their willingness to recommend it
pool.explain: Customers are grouped into promoters, passives and detractors.
pool.evidence: Net Promoter Score (NPS) is a method of calculating how customers are talking about your company and their willingness to recommend your organization to others.

pool.q: In NPS terms, how do passives behave?
options: They won't go out of their way to recommend the business
They urge others to stay away
pool.explain: Detractors, by contrast, may urge others not to come.
pool.evidence: Passives are not likely to go out of their way to recommend the business

pool.q: What is total quality management (TQM) in tourism and hospitality?
options: The whole team, managers and employees, setting service expectations together
pool.explain: TQM is collaborative rather than top-down.
pool.evidence: is a process where service expectations are created by the entire team, with a collaborative approach between management and employees

pool.q: How can great service sometimes be delivered?
options: By doing everything for every guest
By empowering guests to take action themselves
pool.explain: Some guests prefer a link or an app so they can research options on their own.
pool.evidence: Sometimes great service is provided by empowering the guest to take action themselves

pool.q: Why is training critical in customer service?
options: It replaces the need for managers
It ensures quality service and meets service objectives
It is required only for new hires
It lets staff skip customer feedback
pool.explain: Recognised training also helps with recruitment, retention and engagement.
pool.evidence: Training is critical to ensuring quality service and meeting these objectives

pool.q: When you receive feedback, what should you try to do first?
options: Suspend your reaction until you understand what is being said
Ask someone else for their opinion
pool.explain: Feedback can sound like criticism; understanding comes before responding.
pool.evidence: Attempt to suspend your reaction until you understand the information that is being given.

pool.q: What should you do before giving someone feedback?
options: Wait until the person is stressed
Gather all the facts you can
pool.explain: Facts help avoid misunderstanding and keep feedback fair.
pool.evidence: Search out all the facts you can prior to giving your feedback.

pool.q: When is user research actually useful?
options: Only if your team can use what you've learned to improve the service
Only when it is published as a report
Only when the sample is very large
Only at the end of a project
pool.explain: Share findings regularly — ideally at a fixed time each week or sprint.
pool.evidence: User research is only useful if your team can use what you’ve learned to improve your service.
